typeBreakdown.notes: Ischaemic stroke accounts for 62% of all incident strokes, while hemorrhagic strokes drive disproportionate early mortality.

riskFactors.title: High Blood Pressure
riskFactors.description: Hypertension contributes to over 50% of all ischaemic and hemorrhagic strokes.

riskFactors.title: Smoking & Tobacco
riskFactors.description: Doubles the risk of ischaemic stroke and increases hemorrhagic risk.

riskFactors.title: Atrial Fibrillation
riskFactors.description: Increases stroke risk 5-fold; causes cardiogenic emboli.

riskFactors.title: High LDL Cholesterol
riskFactors.description: Drives carotid artery atherosclerosis and plaque rupture.

riskFactors.title: Diabetes Mellitus
riskFactors.description: Increases stroke risk 2-fold and worsens acute post-stroke outcomes.

riskFactors.title: Obesity & Inactivity
riskFactors.description: Elevates blood pressure, blood glucose, and systemic vascular inflammation.

riskFactors.title: Carotid Artery Stenosis
riskFactors.description: Atherosclerotic plaque accumulation in carotid arteries increases ischemic stroke risk.

riskFactors.title: Oral Contraceptive Use
riskFactors.description: Estrogen-containing contraceptives combined with smoking elevate thrombotic risk.

didYouKnow: 1 in 4 adults over age 25 will experience a stroke in their lifetime.
Up to 90% of strokes are preventable by targeting 10 modifiable risk factors.
FAST warning signs (Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call 911) save millions of brain cells.
Over 85% of all stroke deaths occur in low- and middle-income countries.

faq.q: How many stroke deaths occur worldwide every year?
faq.a: According to the World Stroke Organization, stroke claims approximately 6.7 million lives annually, making it the second leading single cause of death worldwide.

faq.q: What is the difference between ischaemic and hemorrhagic stroke?
faq.a: An ischaemic stroke (~62% of cases) occurs when a blood clot blocks an artery to the brain. A hemorrhagic stroke (~38% of cases) occurs when a brain blood vessel ruptures.
Yes. Up to 90% of strokes are linked to 10 modifiable risk factors, primarily high blood pressure, smoking, diabetes, high cholesterol, and physical inactivity.
